title: Production of documents or other things
summary: A court or the officer in charge of a police station may seek production of a document, electronic communication, device, or other thing when needed for a covered proceeding. The provision includes exceptions and addresses how the requirement may be fulfilled.

title: Audio-video recording of search and seizure
summary: The provision requires recording specified searches and seizures using audio-video electronic means, including preparation of the list and witness signatures, and forwarding the record to the designated magistrate without delay.

title: Power to seize certain property
summary: A police officer may seize property alleged or suspected to be stolen, or whose discovery raises suspicion of an offence. The section specifies reporting requirements, including a report to the jurisdictional magistrate. Verify applicability before any bank-account action.

title: Information in cognizable cases
summary: Information about a cognizable offence may be given orally or electronically to the officer in charge, irrespective of where it occurred. The section specifies how each form is recorded, including signature within three days for electronic information.

title: Forensic examination of qualifying crime scenes
summary: For offences punishable by seven years or more, the section provides for a forensic expert to collect crime-scene evidence and for recording of the process, subject to the relevant state notification and provisions on access to facilities.

title: Custody limits and default bail
summary: The provision sets a 90-day ceiling in cases involving death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment for ten years or more, and 60 days for other offences. On expiry, it conditions release on the accused being prepared to furnish, and furnishing, bail.

title: Investigation without unnecessary delay
summary: An investigation under the chapter must be completed without unnecessary delay. The section has additional provisions for certain offences and reporting. It does not establish a single universal chargesheet deadline for fraud cases.

title: Police report and electronic-device custody
summary: After the investigation is completed, the officer in charge forwards the police report to the competent magistrate in the prescribed form. Among the required particulars is the custody sequence for any electronic device.

title: Progress update for the informant or victim
summary: The police officer must inform the informant or victim of investigation progress within 90 days. The provision allows electronic communication. Confirm the case-specific anchor before using a demo reminder.

title: Cheating
summary: The section defines cheating through deception and resulting inducement, and distinguishes the consequences and punishment for different forms, including dishonest inducement to deliver property.

title: Cheating by personation
summary: Cheating by pretending to be another person, substituting one person for another, or misrepresenting identity is addressed by this section.

title: Identity theft
summary: This provision covers dishonest or fraudulent use of another person's electronic signature, password, or other unique identification feature.

title: Cheating by personation via computer resources
summary: The provision addresses cheating by personation by means of a communication device or computer resource.

title: Admissibility of electronic records
summary: The provision sets conditions for proving an electronic record through computer output. Subsection (4) and the Schedule address the required certificate when submitting such a record.
